decidedBy: the project owner, 2026-10-12: Esau had two Canaanite wives and one daughter of Ishmael, and the other identities are to be decided as is most logical; applied by an agent (claude-opus-5-5) reading Genesis 26:34, 28:9 and 36:2-3 on his instruction
policy: Esau's wives are named twice, in Genesis 26:34 and 28:9 and again in 36:2-3. Where both lists give a woman the same father, she is one woman under two names: Bashemath daughter of Elon is Adah, and Mahalath daughter of Ishmael is the Bashemath of 36:3, and each pair is folded into one record. Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Aholibamah daughter of Anah the Hivite have different fathers and peoples and stay two records, each saying that some commentators identify them.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's decision of 2026-10-12 on Esau's wives, applied by claude-opus-5-5

says.notes: Genesis 26:34 and 28:9 name Esau's wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite and Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebajoth; Genesis 36:2-3 names them Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite, and Bashemath Ishmael's daughter, the sister of Nebajoth. Adah is the Bashemath daughter of Elon of 26:34 under another name: both lists give her father as Elon the Hittite.

rulings.why: 'Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite' (GEN 36:2) is the 'Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite' of GEN 26:34: the same father and the same place among Esau's wives.

rulings.why: 'Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth' (GEN 28:9) is the 'Bashemath Ishmael's daughter, sister of Nebajoth' of GEN 36:3.

Whether Judith is Aholibamah of 36:2 under another name the text does not say. Some commentators hold that Judith and Aholibamah are one woman.

rulings.why: 'Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite' (GEN 26:34). Her father and her people are not Aholibamah's, and the identification some commentators make is said on the record.

says.notes: Genesis 26:34 and 28:9 name Esau's wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite and Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebajoth; Genesis 36:2-3 names them Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite, and Bashemath Ishmael's daughter, the sister of Nebajoth. Whether Aholibamah is Judith of 26:34 under another name the text does not say: the two lists name her father differently, Beeri the Hittite and Anah the Hivite, and Genesis 36:24 makes Anah the son of Zibeon. Some commentators hold that Aholibamah and Judith are one woman.

rulings.why: 'Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite' (GEN 36:2). Her father and her people are not Judith's, and the identification some commentators make is said on the record.
